newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE'S DEVELOPMENT HINGES ON INFRASTRUCTURE - MIN.
newsitem.headline: GREECE'S DEVELOPMENT HINGES ON INFRASTRUCTURE - MIN.

text.p: Greece's development hinges on improved infrastructure, the success of its EU convergence plan and a climate of confidence created by economic stability, Development Minister Vasso Papandreou said.

With traditional safeguard methods such as devaluation and taxation being eliminated, Greece must boost its infrastructure and improve its production methods to compete in a modern international market, she told an ecomomic conference.
"This way the Greek economy will participate in the international competitive environment, avoiding marginalisation and stagnation," Papandreou said.

Greece's development programme does not only aim to reach quantitative targets but to bring quality to its markets by introducing new industries, retraining personnel and increasing employment, she said.
Development cannot be achieved unless it goes hand-in-hand with stability and public confidence in the economy, she added.

"The successful implementation of the convergence programme with a drop in inflation and interest rates, significantly improved the investement climate and allowed the successful implementation of the development programme," she said.

The socialist government's 14 trillion drachma development programme spans a period between 1994 and 1999. The private sector is expected to contribute about 2.0 to 3.0 trillion, the EU another six and the state will put up the rest, she said. --Dina Kyriakidou, Intercontinental Press room, +301 9206370
